overall_reason: A two-section v0-style SaaS skeleton (pill badge, two-line 'Stop X. Start Y.' hero with the second line in brand blue, mock product card, avatar-initials social proof, 01/02/03 step cards) with no footer and nothing that belongs to this product beyond the tool names in the mock.

findings.evidence: Failed T-DEFAULT-AGENT: pill badge with sparkle icon 'A better way to discover AI', h1 'Stop searching. / Start building.' with the second line coloured #1d4ed8, primary + ghost button pair, overlapping initial avatars 'A S M J', and a floating mock card on the right. Every element is the stock v0/shadcn landing hero; dom meta generator is 'v0.app'.
findings.before: "Stop searching. Start building." + pill badge + mock card + avatar row
findings.after: A hero built around the actual job: e.g. the goal picker itself (goal, budget, comfort level) live in the first screen, so the visitor starts using it instead of reading about it
findings.why: The whole first screen is a category template; swap the product and nothing changes.

findings.evidence: Failed T-RIVAL-NAME: 'Stop searching. Start building.' and 'Less browsing. More doing.' stay true for any tool directory, no-code builder or productivity app. Both use the same two-fragment antithesis.
findings.before: "Stop searching. Start building." / "Less browsing. More doing."
findings.after: A head only this product can say, e.g. what the stack recommendation is based on [DATA NEEDED: how the matching works, how many tools are covered]
findings.why: The headline does no work; the paired-fragment formula repeats across both headings (T-OVER-CORRECTION substitute habit).

findings.evidence: Failed T-STOCK-ORDER: three equal white cards labelled 01 / 02 / 03 with 'Tell us what you want to do', 'Get your personalized stack', 'Make something great'; the card bodies are one line each and the third ('Follow the steps and start building today.') says nothing. Section order: badge hero + mock, 1-2-3 steps, end. No footer.
findings.before: 01 Tell us what you want to do / 02 Get your personalized stack / 03 Make something great
findings.after: Show one worked example end to end (goal in, stack out with why each tool was picked) instead of three abstract steps
findings.why: Equal step cards are the default explanation section; 'Make something great' fails T-THREE-LINE (not picturable, not falsifiable, not specific).

findings.evidence: Coloured initial avatars 'A', 'S', 'M', 'J' stacked next to the count: placeholder faces standing in for people. (The '12,000+' count itself is a sweep hit.)
findings.before: Four letter-avatar circles + 'Trusted by 12,000+ curious builders'
findings.after: Remove the avatar stack; show real users only with consent [DATA NEEDED: real user count and source]
findings.why: Letter avatars are fake-people filler that imply a crowd the page cannot show.

findings.evidence: Failed T-DELETION: 'YOUR PERSONALIZED STACK' caps label, 'Ready to go' green status pill, and 01-04 numbers on each tool row add nothing; letter tiles 'C', 'CC', '11' stand in for real tool logos. At 375px the 'Ready to go' pill wraps and clips ('Ready to / go').
findings.before: Mock card with status pill, row numbers and initial tiles
findings.after: Show the recommendation with the reason each tool was chosen and its own price, drop the row numbers and the status pill
findings.why: Decorative dashboard chrome makes the mock look like a component demo rather than this product's output.

findings.evidence: Page is 1228px tall at 1440: hero plus one three-card section, no footer, no tool list, no pricing, no about. Nav items 'AI tools', 'Compare', 'About' are <button>s with no href.
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: real tool catalogue, comparison content, who runs this] and a footer with contact and ownership
findings.why: A thin page with dead nav reads as a generated shell, not a product site; the visitor's job (pick tools) has no content to act on.

strengths: The hero mock names concrete tools (ChatGPT, Canva, CapCut, ElevenLabs) and a rupee monthly cost, which hints at a real local audience; keep that specificity.
Sub-line 'Tell us the goal. We'll build the stack.' states the mechanism plainly.
not_investigated: Behaviour of the goal picker behind 'Find my AI stack' (not captured)
Brand brief: no contract overrides supplied
